chapter: Childhood and first bands in Ohio
title: Buying a violin and studying with Mark Snyder
summary: At eleven or twelve he buys a violin with his lamp-lighting pay, gets lessons from a Cincinnati Symphony violinist and plays solos with the school orchestra.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: Sure, Just a Song at Twilight.
And you learned to read. Yeah, uh-huh.

So then I didn't like that. So they started to having music in the schools, public schools, so I figured, I said, "Now I've got to have something to play." So I saw this violin in the arcade at home. $16. And I was at a job lighting gas lamps, so I bought --
How old were you then about?

And I -- My mother, I used to give her my check every payday. But I saw this violin and she was standing upon a corner waiting for me to give her the check, but I had slipped around the arcade music store at home in Springfield and I got this violin. And it was a funny looking case. It looked like you put a dead person in.

A wooden case. So I had the violin in there and I came around and my mother looked and saw this violin case, so she tried to get mad because I didn't have the check, but she had to smile. So I took the violin home and I told Professor [Humberger,] he was supervisor of music at

home in the schools, and I told him I wanted to play the violin. So he sent me to a teacher, Mark Snyder. He used to play a second violin in the Cincinnati Symphony. And I took lessons from him and I got so I could play a lot of things on the violin. It got so I could play solos in front of the orchestra. I could play Souvenir, da-da-da-de de-de, things like that.
The only thing whipped me was Caprice Vieuxtemps when I tried to tackle that.
Oh, was he. He was beautiful. You know, I got to hear him in person.
